subject: deepagents
title: Library-core scoring convention: loop lives in upstream langchain create_agent; the in-tree middleware assembly is the scoreable architecture, capped at 8
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/graph.py:11 (import create_agent), graph.py:961 (return create_agent(...middleware=deepagent_middleware)), graph.py:259-269 (required-middleware protection), graph.py:615-623 (_verify_excluded_middleware_coverage)
one_why: Dispatcher-mandated ruling for the covariate family (openhands out-of-process, SWE-agent/swerex, kimi vendored libs): credit what the tree enforces around the loop, never the loop itself, and never dock for the loop's absence - symmetric zero-credit/zero-blame with the openhands row; keeps wrapper subjects comparable to full harnesses without letting them claim codex rungs.

subject: deepagents
title: AsyncSubAgentMiddleware launches background subagent tasks on remote Agent Protocol servers, returning task IDs immediately so the main agent keeps working
evidence: libs/deepagents/deepagents/middleware/async_subagents.py:840-850 (start/monitor/update tools, task-ID return), graph.py:50 (AsyncSubAgentMiddleware wired into default stack)
one_why: Corpus-unique orchestration shape: every other subject's subagents are in-process synchronous children; this one is transport-native (any Agent Protocol server, LangGraph Platform or self-hosted FastAPI), which makes cross-host agent trees and crash isolation a deployment property rather than a harness feature.

subject: deepagents
title: Excluding middleware by name is verified for coverage: an exclusion entry matching nothing across main and subagent stacks raises, and required classes are unexcludable
one_why: Config-driven stack trimming normally rots silently when a renamed middleware makes an exclusion string dead - here the dead exclusion fails loudly at construction; cheap anti-drift pattern for any pluggable pipeline, and it doubles as a test that the profile layer still matches the stack.

subject: deepagents
title: CI workflow files are treated as tested artifacts: eval tests parse harbor.yml/_eval.yml themselves, and paths-filter forces any eval-workflow edit to run its guard tests
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:173-186 (paths-filter comment: 'editing any eval workflow must run the evals tests that validate it - otherwise the change skips its guard'); libs/evals/tests/unit_tests/test_harbor_langsmith_integration.py
one_why: The guard against the classic CI bug - a workflow edit that silently opts out of the very job that would catch it - by making the YAML part of the code-under-test; sibling of dvalincode's action-pin-consistency-test, generalizable to any repo whose behavior is partly encoded in pipeline config.
